definitions.gloss: troops and horses; military forces; military matters
definitions.explanation: A literary term referring to soldiers and their horses, used to represent military power or warfare in general. Appears in historical texts, literary works, and formal writing.

examples.japanese: {兵馬|へいば}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{権|けん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{握|にぎ}る→握る：02383_nigiru⟧。
{兵馬|へいば}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{時代|じだい}→時代：01424_jidai⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{終|お}わり、⟦{平和|へいわ}→平和：01507_heiwa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{訪|おとず}れた→訪れる：07678_otozureru⟧。
examples.english: The age of warfare ended, and peace arrived.

examples.japanese: ⟦{戦国|せんごく}→戦国：27122_sengoku⟧⟦{大名|だいみょう}→大名：10378_daimyou⟧たち⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{兵馬|へいば}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{整|ととの}え→整える：04259_totonoeru⟧、⟦{天下統一|てんかとういつ}→天下統一：20946_tenkatouitsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧めざして⟦{争|あらそ}った→争う：01866_arasou⟧。
examples.english: The feudal lords of the Warring States period assembled their military forces and competed for the unification of the country.

notes:
A classical compound of ⟦{兵|へい}→兵：29510_hei⟧ (soldiers) and {馬|ば} (horses), representing military power by synecdoche. In pre-modern warfare, cavalry and infantry were the two pillars of an army, so the pairing evokes the full scope of a military force.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {兵馬|へいば}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{権|けん}: military authority
- {兵馬|へいば}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{動|うご}かす→動かす：01885_ugokasu⟧: mobilize forces
- {兵馬|へいば}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{整|ととの}える→整える：04259_totonoeru⟧: prepare military forces
- {兵馬|へいば}{俑|よう}: terracotta army (the famous Chinese burial figures)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {軍勢|ぐんぜい}: military force; army (more concrete, refers to actual troops)
- ⟦{軍事|ぐんじ}→軍事：14392_gunji⟧: military affairs (modern, administrative term)
- ⟦{武力|ぶりょく}→武力：13221_buryoku⟧: military power; armed force (modern term for the concept of force)

REGISTER:
Primarily a literary and historical term. In modern Japanese, it appears mainly in historical writing, classical literature, and discussions of East Asian history. The compound {兵馬|へいば}{俑|よう} (terracotta warriors) is perhaps its most widely known modern usage.
